content.value_statement: Protein research teams need clear guidance for ESM3, ESM C, and Forge workflows. This skill organizes model selection, generation, embeddings, and output handling for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains ESM3 sequence, structure, and function generation workflows.
Shows ESM C embedding extraction for downstream protein analysis.
Compares local ESM models with Forge-hosted model options.
Provides examples for inverse folding, batch processing, and caching.
Documents output formats such as PDB, FASTA, and embedding arrays.
Covers error handling, rate limits, and model selection tradeoffs.
limitations: Generated proteins require expert review, biosafety review, and experimental validation.
Forge workflows require user-managed API access and may send data to a remote service.
Local models need suitable Python dependencies, memory, and GPU resources.
The skill provides guidance and examples, not guaranteed biological performance.

use_cases.title: Prototype protein designs
use_cases.description: Generate candidate sequences, refine structures, and compare model settings before laboratory planning.

use_cases.title: Build embedding analyses
use_cases.description: Create ESM C embeddings for clustering, classification, similarity search, or property prediction.

use_cases.title: Scale Forge workflows
use_cases.description: Plan remote inference, batching, retry handling, and result caching for larger protein workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a first sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ESM3 to complete this masked protein sequence: [sequence]. Explain model choice, generation settings, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create embeddings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ESM C for these protein sequences: [sequences]. Recommend model size, batching approach, and downstream analysis options.

prompt_templates.title: Design from structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inverse folding with this target structure file: [path]. Outline the workflow, constraints, outputs, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Forge batch inference
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Forge API batch workflow for [number] proteins. Include model choice, retry handling, caching, rate limits, and privacy cautions.

output_examples.input: Complete a masked protein sequence with ESM3.
output: Recommended an ESM3 model and generation track.
Explained mask handling, temperature, and validation steps.
Listed expected outputs such as sequence and predicted structure.

output_examples.input: Compare ESM C models for embedding a variant library.
output: Compared speed, memory needs, and representation quality.
Suggested batching and cache strategy for repeated analysis.
Outlined clustering and property prediction uses.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Forge API workflow for many protein prompts.
output: Selected a hosted model for the workload.
Outlined retries, rate limits, and checkpointing.
Added privacy cautions for proprietary sequences and tokens.

best_practices: Start with smaller models, then repeat promising designs with larger models.
Keep Forge tokens outside prompts and source files.
Validate generated proteins with independent tools, expert review, and responsible biodesign checks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated sequences as experimentally safe without review.
Do not send proprietary sequences to remote APIs without approval.
Do not use large models before defining constraints, metrics, and validation criteria.

faq.question: Can this skill run ESM models by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples. The user still needs the ESM package, model access, and compute.

faq.question: Does it support local and remote inference?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers local open models and Forge API workflows when the user has proper access.

faq.question: What inputs can I use?
faq.answer: Typical inputs include protein sequences, masked regions, structures, function annotations, and model selection constraints.

faq.question: Can it replace laboratory validation?
faq.answer: No. Generated designs need expert review, biosafety review, and experimental validation before use.

faq.question: How should I handle Forge API tokens?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or a secret manager. Avoid placing tokens in prompts, notebooks, or shared files.

faq.question: Is this suitable for non-experts?
faq.answer: It can explain workflows, but protein design decisions require qualified scientific oversight.
